study.trial_id: exenatide QW plus metformin in PCOS (Chin Med J 2021, NCT04029272)
study.comparator: metformin 500 mg three times daily alone
study.notes: STUDY: open label prospective randomised two arm trial, Peking Union Medical College Hospital, 50 overweight or obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome (Rotterdam criteria) randomised 25 and 25 by a computer generated two block procedure to metformin 500 mg three times daily (MET) or the same metformin plus exenatide 2 mg once weekly (COM) for 12 weeks; 40 of 50 (80 per cent) completed and Tables 2 and 3 are the per protocol completers, 21 MET and 19 COM. HELD under amendment A6: the defining population is polycystic ovary syndrome, outside the population criterion, with overweight or obesity required for entry (baseline BMI 30.4 and 30.8 kg/m2), so the group is extracted in full and held with groups 202, 44, 200 and 205 rather than excluded by the extractor. ROUTE: Table 3 prints the per arm change as mean plus or minus SD with the between group P, and its sign convention is PRE MINUS POST, verified against the Table 2 pre and post values on three markers (weight 79.10 to 77.05 in MET printed as 2.05; ApoA1 1.25 to 1.65 printed as minus 0.40; fasting insulin 20.50 to 21.81 in MET printed as minus 1.31), so every Table 3 value is entered here negated into the post minus pre convention of the pipeline. Baseline means and SDs are Table 2 pre treatment, which gives the percent scale denominator on the row. DOUBT: Table 2 and Table 3 disagree for COM fasting insulin, 26.55 to 23.0 implies a fall of 3.55 while Table 3 prints 2.43; the change table is used, because it is the source of the dispersion, and the discrepancy is recorded. Markers reported without a usable dispersion: hsCRP, HOMA-IR, HOMA-beta, triglycerides and QUICKI are printed as medians with IQR in both tables and a median change cannot be rescaled to a percent of a mean baseline (A12), so they are listed, not extracted. pct_weight_change minus 2.12 computed by the session: COM lost 3.76 kg and MET 2.05 kg (Table 3), a between arm difference of minus 1.71 kg over the n weighted baseline weight (82.34*19 + 79.10*21)/40 = 80.64 kg, 100*(-1.71)/80.64 = -2.12. prespecified_endpoint FALSE: the primary outcomes were the anthropometric changes, the metabolic parameters were secondary. industry_funded left empty: no funding or conflict statement is present in the captured text, and FALSE would assert a declaration the paper does not make

rows.notes: Table 3 fasting plasma glucose change 0.26 (0.45) COM vs 0.01 (0.31) MET mmol/L printed pre minus post, P = 0.040, entered negated; Table 2 pre 5.21 (0.57) and post 4.93 (0.47) COM, pre 5.20 (0.46) and post 5.19 (0.51) MET

Table 3 fasting insulin change 2.43 (10.23) COM vs minus 1.31 (7.52) MET micro IU/mL printed pre minus post, P = 0.118, entered negated; Table 2 pre 26.55 (14.70) and post 23.0 (10.16) COM implies a fall of 3.55, which Table 3 prints as 2.43, a discrepancy of 1.12 between the paper's own tables that is recorded and not reconciled by the extractor

Table 3 total cholesterol change minus 0.18 (0.87) COM vs minus 0.49 (0.80) MET mmol/L printed pre minus post, so cholesterol ROSE in both arms, P = 0.270, entered negated; Table 2 pre 4.94 (0.78) to post 5.13 (0.99) COM and pre 5.15 (0.87) to post 5.64 (0.88) MET confirms the rise in both arms

Table 3 LDL cholesterol change 0.23 (0.75) COM vs 0.01 (0.68) MET mmol/L printed pre minus post, P = 0.328, entered negated; Table 2 pre 3.22 (0.61) to post 2.98 (0.83) COM and pre 3.38 (0.71) to post 3.37 (0.78) MET

json.design: randomised open label parallel two arm, per protocol completers analysed
json.reason: population polycystic ovary syndrome with overweight or obesity (NCT04029272, Chin Med J 2021, exenatide 2 mg once weekly plus metformin vs metformin alone, 12 weeks), held under amendment A6 with groups 202, 44, 200 and 205; four rows are staged and ready to enter the master if the Director admits the population
tables_used: Table 2 baseline and 12 week per arm
Table 3 per arm change with between group P

rob.justification: d1 low: computer generated two block randomisation with an average of 25 per group. d2 high: open label, and the comparator is metformin alone against metformin plus an injected agonist, so neither participants nor investigators are blinded in a trial whose primary outcome is weight. d3 high: 10 of 50 randomised did not complete and the analysis in Tables 2 and 3 is per protocol with no imputation, 21 and 19 of 25 and 25. d4 low: laboratory assays. d5 some_concerns: the metabolic markers are secondary outcomes, the registration is NCT04029272 and the captured text does not state which of them were registered

doubts: Table 2 and Table 3 disagree for COM fasting insulin (fall of 3.55 from Table 2 against 2.43 in Table 3); the change table is used and the discrepancy recorded

Table 3 prints reductions as positive numbers (pre minus post), the opposite of the pipeline convention, so every value is negated here; the convention was verified on weight, ApoA1 and MET fasting insulin against Table 2
no funding or conflict of interest statement is present in the captured text
the first author is not in the captured text and is left empty rather than guessed
